venues.name: The Chedi Muscat
venues.area: Al Ghubra North, Shatti Al Qurum
venues.note: GHM's serene, minimalist beachfront sanctuary, the hotel that defined understated luxury in the Gulf, and Oman's one true icon.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards, #4 Hotel in the Middle East (2025); #1 Hotel in the Middle East (2024)
World Travel Awards, World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)

venues.name: Mandarin Oriental, Muscat
venues.note: The group's Oman debut, a bright-white beachfront house where Omani craft meets Mandarin Oriental's quiet precision.
credentials: Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group (Leading maison group; Forbes Travel Guide inspected, 'soon to be rated')
Opened June 2024, the brand's first hotel in Oman

venues.name: Al Husn, a Waldorf Astoria Hotel
venues.note: An adults-oriented clifftop 'castle' above a private turquoise cove, the crown of the Barr Al Jissah headland, now under the Waldorf Astoria flag.
credentials: Waldorf Astoria Hotels & Resorts, Oman debut of the brand (rebranded from Shangri-La Al Husn, 1 Jan 2026; Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star as Shangri-La Al Husn)
Part of the landmark Barr Al Jissah resort complex

venues.name: The St. Regis Al Mouj Muscat Resort
venues.note: A polished beachfront newcomer beside Muscat's smartest marina-and-golf community, St. Regis butler service and a long private beach.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
World Travel Awards, World's Leading New Resort (2025); Oman's Leading Luxury Resort (2025)

venues.name: Kempinski Hotel Muscat
venues.note: A vast six-kilometre-beachfront European grande-dame resort, eleven dining venues and a private stretch of sand at Al Mouj.
credentials: Kempinski Hotels, recognised in Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards (2025)
World Travel Awards, Oman's Leading Beach Resort; Business Traveller Middle East, Best Business Hotel in Muscat

venues.name: W Muscat
venues.note: The brand's beachfront 'W Escape', high-design, high-energy and unabashedly scene-y, right on Shatti Al Qurum.
credentials: Marriott W Hotels (design-forward luxury brand); W Muscat is the brand's Oman debut
Luxury Lifestyle Awards, Luxury Lifestyle Hotel, Oman (2024)

venues.name: The Restaurant, The Chedi Muscat
venues.area: The Chedi Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
venues.note: Four open kitchens, Arabic, Indian, Asian and Mediterranean, under one high, chandeliered ceiling; the Chedi's flagship all-day room.
credentials: Within The Chedi Muscat (Forbes 4-Star; World Travel Awards World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa)

venues.name: The Beach Restaurant, The Chedi Muscat
venues.area: The Chedi Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
venues.note: Sand-underfoot seafood by the Gulf, Iranian and Caspian caviar, freshly shucked oysters and the line-caught catch of the day.
credentials: Within The Chedi Muscat (Forbes 4-Star; World Travel Awards World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa)

venues.name: Al Angham
venues.area: Royal Opera House Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
venues.note: The finest room dedicated to Omani cuisine, carved-plaster grandeur beside the Opera House, serving the sultanate's own dishes with real ceremony.
credentials: Set within the Royal Opera House Muscat cultural complex, Oman's flagship dedicated fine-dining Omani restaurant

venues.name: Bukhara, Kempinski Hotel Muscat
venues.note: Robust North Indian cooking from the clay tandoor, inside the city's largest beach resort, familiar flavours, done with polish.
credentials: Within Kempinski Hotel Muscat (Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice 2025; World Travel Awards Oman's Leading Beach Resort)

venues.name: Shahi Darbar (fine Indian dining)
venues.note: Long-standing, well-regarded North Indian kitchen with a devoted local following, generous, familiar, unfussy.
credentials: Established Muscat Indian restaurant with a consistent local reputation

venues.name: Ubhar
venues.area: Bareeq Al Shatti, Shatti Al Qurum
venues.note: Modern Omani-and-Arabian cooking that treats the sultanate's home dishes seriously, shuwa, harees, camel, done with pride.
credentials: Widely cited (Time Out Muscat and others) as Muscat's leading modern Omani restaurant

venues.name: Kargeen Café
venues.note: Lantern-lit garden courtyards and generous Omani-Levantine mezze, the city's most-loved relaxed table, buzzing past midnight.
credentials: An enduring Muscat institution, widely recommended for atmosphere and authentic mezze

venues.name: Bin Ateeq
venues.note: Floor-seated, private-room dining on Omani classics, shuwa and majboos served the old way, with no ceremony and real honesty.
credentials: Long-established local institution for authentic traditional Omani cuisine

venues.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
venues.note: Oman's grandest mosque and the one unmissable landmark of Muscat, 300,000 tonnes of Indian sandstone, a single hand-woven Persian carpet that took years to make, and a Swarovski chandelier hanging under the main dome. Non-Muslim visitors are welcome between 8 and 11 in the morning (not Fridays); entry is free, dress is modest, and abayas are lent at the gate. Serene and spotless, an easy, moving stop for all generations.

venues.name: Royal Opera House Muscat
venues.note: The Gulf's leading opera house, Omani stone and marble outside, Islamic, Mughal and European craftsmanship within. Either take a daytime house tour of the auditorium and its inlaid detail, or book an evening of opera, ballet or orchestral music from the October–May season. A refined, dressy night out that families and culture-minded couples both love.

venues.name: Mutrah Corniche
venues.note: The great curving seafront of old Muscat, whitewashed merchant houses on one side, dhows and the Sultan's harbour on the other, the Hajar hills behind. Walk it late afternoon into golden hour when the light softens and the mosque minarets glow. The gentle, unhurried heart of the city.

venues.name: Mutrah Souq
venues.note: One of the oldest markets in the Arab world, a warren of covered lanes trading frankincense, silver khanjars, pashminas, antique silver and Omani halwa. Prices are gentle by Dubai standards and the traders are warm, not pushy, good for unhurried, multi-generation browsing. Best late afternoon into the evening when it reopens and comes alive.

venues.name: Mutrah Fish Market
venues.note: A working morning market under a striking wave-form roof on the harbour, where Omani fishermen land and sell the day's catch. Come at dawn for the full theatre of it, kingfish, tuna and hammour changing hands amid the calls of the auction. Vivid, authentic, and a photographer's delight.

venues.name: Al Alam Palace
venues.note: The Sultan's ceremonial palace, flamboyant gold-and-blue flared columns framed by manicured avenues, designed by Mumbai's Shapoorji Pallonji firm. You cannot go inside, but the grand approach and the palace flanked by two Portuguese forts is the classic Muscat photograph. A short, easy stop paired with Old Muscat's museums.

venues.name: Al Jalali & Al Mirani Forts
venues.note: Two 16th-century Portuguese forts guarding the natural harbour on either side of Al Alam Palace. Neither is generally open to the public, but they crown the rocky headlands and give Old Muscat its dramatic, defensible silhouette. Best seen from the palace forecourt or the corniche, especially at dusk.

venues.name: National Museum of Oman
venues.note: Oman's flagship museum, opposite Al Alam Palace, beautifully lit galleries of the ruling dynasty, Omani silver, frankincense trade, arms and maritime heritage, with Arabic Braille throughout. Cool, calm and well-curated: the single best hour for understanding the country before you explore it. Excellent for curious teenagers.

venues.name: Bait Al Zubair Museum
venues.note: A private family museum in a cluster of traditional houses, the finest privately held collection of Omani khanjars, jewellery, costume and household life, plus a garden, café and art gallery. Intimate and personal where the National Museum is grand; the two together tell the whole story. On Al Saidiya Street in Old Muscat.

venues.name: Ghalya's Museum of Modern Art
venues.note: A quiet gem on the Mutrah corniche, a reconstructed Omani house recreating daily life from 1950 to 1975, room by room, with a small modern-art gallery upstairs. Founded by a member of the royal family, it is warm, unhurried and rarely crowded. A tender, human counterpoint to the big state museums.

venues.name: Old Muscat walking circuit
venues.note: The walled original town behind the corniche, palace, forts, museums, the old Muscat Gate and quiet lanes, all within a compact, walkable radius. A morning here, with a private guide to unlock the history, gives you the founding story of the whole city in a couple of unhurried hours. Shaded stops and easy pacing suit all ages.

venues.name: Amouage Perfume Factory & Visitor Centre
venues.note: The home of Oman's luxury house of perfume, built on frankincense, myrrh and Omani rose. A complimentary guided tour walks you from raw ingredient to finished bottle, ending in a boutique where you can sample and buy the full collection. A civilised, air-conditioned hour and a genuinely Omani luxury souvenir. Sunday to Thursday, mornings and afternoons.

venues.name: Dolphin watching by boat
venues.note: Morning boats slip out of the marina to meet wild spinner and common dolphins that ride the bow and leap in their hundreds along this coast. A short, easy two-hour trip, thrilling for children and grandparents alike, with the fort-studded shoreline as backdrop. Best in the calm, cool morning sea.

venues.name: Sunset dhow cruise
venues.note: Sail the coast at dusk aboard a traditional wooden dhow, past cliffs, coves and the lights of Muscat coming on. Private charters can be arranged with Omani coffee, dates and dinner aboard, a discreet, romantic way to end a day. The gentlest luxury on the water.

venues.name: Bandar Khayran
venues.note: A hidden labyrinth of turquoise inlets, cliffs and mangroves southeast of the city, 'the blue lagoons', reached by boat or the coast road. Kayak or snorkel the sheltered bays by day, or take a sunset paddle through bioluminescent plankton in winter, when each stroke lights the water. Wild, unspoilt and private-feeling.

venues.name: Qurum Beach
venues.note: A long, clean city beach backed by luxury hotels and the corniche, easy walking, calm swimming and a string of cafés and restaurants. The relaxed everyday beach of Muscat, good for an early stroll or a sunset with the family. Between the Chedi and the Crowne Plaza cliff.

venues.name: Qurum Natural Park
venues.note: The city's largest green park, lakes, lawns, shaded walks, playgrounds and a rose garden set behind the beach. A cool, family-friendly escape for an evening, popular with local families. Simple, safe and easy with young children or grandparents.

venues.name: Afternoon tea at The Chedi Muscat
venues.note: Oman's most stylish resort, long reflecting pools, minimalist Omani-Zen design and a serene Lobby Lounge that serves an exquisite afternoon tea. Even non-residents can book in for tea or dinner and soak up the calm. Discreet luxury of exactly the kind that beats Dubai's glitz. Vegetarian and dietary requests handled with ease.

venues.name: Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel
venues.note: A landmark hotel set between mountains and a private bay, with a soaring 38-metre domed atrium lobby. Come for afternoon tea beneath the dome or a beachfront dinner even if you stay elsewhere, one of Muscat's grand, gracious dining experiences. The setting alone is worth the drive.
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Recommended (2025)
World Travel Awards, World's Leading Palace Hotel (2018)
Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice, Top-5 Hotel in the Middle East (2018)

venues.name: Nizwa Fort & Souq
venues.note: The old imamate capital, 90 minutes inland, a massive 17th-century round-towered fort you can climb for sweeping views, beside a restored souq trading silver, dates, pottery and frankincense. The cultural heart of Oman's interior, and an easy, rewarding day trip with a private car. Best paired with the Friday goat market.

venues.name: Jabreen Castle
venues.note: The most beautiful of Oman's castles, a 1670 palace-fort with painted wooden ceilings, hidden chambers, date-store rooms and a canal running through it. Small, intimate and gorgeously preserved, it rewards a slow wander. An easy pairing with Bahla Fort just up the road.

venues.name: Bahla Fort
venues.note: Oman's only UNESCO-listed fort, a vast 13th-century mud-brick citadel with a 12km oasis wall, steeped in local legend. Recently restored, it is monumental and atmospheric, the great fortress of the interior. Combine with neighbouring Jabreen Castle and Nizwa for a full interior day.
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Bahla Fort

venues.name: Alila Jabal Akhdar
venues.note: A serene stone-built retreat perched on the mountain plateau, all clean lines, big views and a spa above the clouds. The mountain base of choice for couples and families wanting quiet luxury, mountain walks and cool nights. Stay a night to feel Oman's other, alpine self.
credentials: World Travel Awards, Oman's Leading Resort (2023, 2024); Middle East's Leading Boutique Hotel (multiple years)
Condé Nast Traveler Hot List (2015, on opening); first LEED-certified hotel in Oman

venues.name: Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar
venues.note: The highest five-star resort in the Middle East, on the very lip of a canyon with a dramatic cliff-edge pool and rose-ritual spa. Refined, warm and spectacular, guided rose-farm and mountain-guru walks included. A destination in its own right for a multi-generation stay.

venues.name: Wahiba Sands (Sharqiya Sands)
venues.note: A sea of amber dunes over 100m tall, home to the Bedu. Ride the crests by 4x4, meet a Bedouin family, then sleep in a luxury desert camp under a spread of stars with dinner over the fire. The classic Arabian desert night, thrilling for children, magical for all. Book a tented camp with private, comfortable suites.

venues.name: Wadi Bani Khalid
venues.note: The most accessible of Oman's great wadis, emerald spring-fed pools among palms and smooth boulders, a five-minute walk from the car park, with a café overlooking the water. Swim in the warm rock pools or stroll the gorge; there is even a cave for the adventurous. Family-easy and gorgeous. Pairs with a Wahiba desert night.

venues.name: Wadi Shab
venues.note: Oman's most celebrated wadi hike, a short boat across the mouth, then an easy trail past turquoise pools to a hidden cave waterfall you swim to reach. About two hours from Muscat and doable in a day. Bring water shoes; the reward at the end is unforgettable. Best for active families and couples.

venues.name: Rustaq Fort
venues.note: One of Oman's largest forts in a former capital, with towering walls, a mosque and its own hot spring within. Less visited than Nizwa, so often quiet, and paired naturally with Nakhal on the Batinah loop. A grand, uncrowded fort day for history-lovers.

venues.name: Jebel Sifah
venues.note: A resort marina town on the coast south of Muscat, ringed by mountains and a long sandy beach with calm swimming and a golf course. An easy, laid-back seaside escape, kayaking, boat trips and quiet sand within an hour of the city. Good for a relaxed family day by the water.

venues.name: Yiti Beach
venues.note: A wild, quiet cove reached over the coastal hills from Muscat, with a hidden stretch that feels like a private beach. Big skies, few people and mountains meeting the sea, a favourite for a peaceful picnic or sunset drive. Best with a 4x4 and no fixed plans.

venues.name: Muscat Gate & city viewpoints
venues.note: The old ceremonial gate marking the entrance to Old Muscat, near the giant Riyam incense-burner monument on its hill. Climb for a panorama over the corniche, harbour and forts, a quick, free stop that frames the whole old city. Lovely near sunset.

venues.name: Private guide & 4x4 grand tour
venues.note: The best way to see Oman: a licensed private driver-guide and a comfortable 4x4 to link the forts, wadis, mountains and desert at your own pace, with the history unlocked and the logistics handled. Dietary needs, including Jain and pure-vegetarian, are easily arranged ahead. Discreet, flexible and ideal for a multi-generation family.

venues.name: The Long Bar, The Chedi Muscat
venues.area: The Chedi Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
venues.note: A hushed, low-lit lounge inside Oman's design icon, considered cocktails and a fireside calm, the most refined drink in the city.
credentials: Within The Chedi Muscat (Forbes 4-Star; World Travel Awards World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa)

venues.name: The bar at Al Husn, a Waldorf Astoria Hotel
venues.note: Clifftop sundowners above a private cove at the crown of the Barr Al Jissah headland, the classic Muscat sunset drink, now under the Waldorf Astoria flag.
credentials: Within Al Husn, a Waldorf Astoria Hotel (Barr Al Jissah landmark; former Forbes 4-Star Shangri-La Al Husn)

venues.name: Duke's Bar, Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel
venues.note: A classic hotel bar beneath the palace's soaring atrium, the grande-dame address for a measured evening drink in Muscat.
credentials: Within Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel (Forbes Recommended; World Travel Awards World's Leading Palace Hotel)
